column4: Hydrographic and Oceanographic Surveys and Nautical Charting- Expanded
column6: Hydrographic  and Oceanographic Surveys and Nautical Charting
column7: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
column8:
The project involves the deployment of NAMRIA ships, launches, and small boats as platforms for conducting hydrographic surveys across the country’s maritime zones. The data gathered through these surveys are processed and used to produce nautical charts and other maritime publications essential for navigation and various maritime activities.

In addition, the project includes tide and tidal current observations, data processing, analysis, and prediction to generate tide and current tables for fisheries and maritime users. NAMRIA also establishes secondary and subordinate tide stations to enhance survey support and collects sea surface temperature, density, and salinity measurements to enrich the physical oceanographic data maintained at the National Oceanographic Data Center (NODC). The NODC provides critical oceanographic information needed for coastal development planning, climate change studies, and disaster risk management.

column4: Resource Assessment and Mapping - Expanded
column6: Resource Assessment and Mapping
column7: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
column8:
The project accelerates the national land cover and coastal resource by reducing the mapping cycle from the current five-year period to a more responsive 2–3 year cycle. Several priority provinces are strategically aligned with the CCAM-DRR Roadmap, reinforcing national efforts on climate change adaptation, mitigation, and disaster risk reduction. From 2025 to 2028, the project will expand to cover eight additional provinces, supporting the production of updated Existing Land Use Maps that strengthen CLUPs, PDPFPs, and address persistent gaps in land management, environmental monitoring, and natural resource governance.
In alignment with its broader objectives, the project will also generate replotted and updated Land Classification (LC) maps overlaid in topographic maps. These enhanced maps correct historical inaccuracies, improve consistency with ground conditions, and serve as a reliable basis for land administration, development planning, environmental protection, and resolving land-related conflicts. They ensure that decisions on land use, titling, and resource management are grounded in precise and up-to-date geospatial information.

The mapping of Safe Open Spaces (SOS) involves updating the SOS of Metro Manila and expanding to the Greater Metro Manila and other high-risk areas by identifying, assessing, and geospatially delineating areas that can serve as secure, accessible evacuation and assembly sites during emergencies or disasters. It includes evaluating site suitability based on safety, capacity, accessibility, environmental conditions, and proximity to at-risk communities. The resulting SOS maps support local governments in disaster preparedness, contingency planning, and resilience-building by providing reliable, location-specific information essential for guiding evacuation planning, resource allocation, and risk-informed decision-making.
The cloud-powered Resource Assessment and Mapping (RAM) Information System is a centralized, online geospatial platform that enables real-time processing, analysis, storage, and sharing of environmental and land resource data. By integrating cloud-based tools such as Google Earth Engine (GEE), the system significantly accelerates geospatial workflows—reducing the mapping cycle for land cover, coastal resources, and land use from several years to a more responsive, data-driven timeframe. It will be integrated into Geoportal Philippines, providing real-time, interoperable, and accessible geospatial data for planners, emergency responders, and stakeholders to enhance earthquake preparedness and sustainable land-use planning. Overall, this initiative advances the availability of critical ENR datasets, enabling evidence-based planning, improved resource management, and informed policy formulation toward a geospatially empowered nation.
These initiatives supports the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals- climate action (SDG 13) through improved disaster preparedness and ecosystem management, promote sustainable cities and communities (SDG 11) by identifying safe and resilient spaces, support life on land (SDG 15) through accurate land and forest management, and strengthen partnerships for sustainable development (SDG 17) by enabling data sharing and informed decision-making across government agencies and stakeholders.

column4: Geospatial Information Management-Expanded
column6: Geospatial Information Management
column7: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
column8:
NAMRIA is mandated to integrate and manage geospatial data to facilitate access, analysis, and conversion into useful information. This project involves the buildup, integration, packaging, sharing, and dissemination of geospatial information utilizing ICT and geographic information system (GIS) technology. The activities under this project include information systems strategic planning, geospatial database management, information systems development, and ICT infrastructure development. The project also provides technical assistance and geomatics training, conducts communication, education and public awareness campaigns, promotions, marketing, and  sustains media relations, publication productions, and client services.

NAMRIA maintains the Geoportal Philippines (GP) accessible at www.geoportal.gov.ph, which is an online platform that manages access and the open sharing of geospatial data holdings of the agency and other stakeholders. To date, the GP hosts various thematic geospatial datasets on geohazards, forestry, mining, environment, road networks, health, and education, among others. It is currently hosted in a cloud environment to ensure efficient access to geospatial information shared by NAMRIA and other stakeholders.

In carrying out its mandate, the agency develops and maintains information systems to strengthen collaboration and data sharing among its technical branches.  These systems are NAMRIA Geospatial Information Management System/NAMRIA Geospatial, which serves as the NAMRIA node linked to the GP, and specific branch nodes connected to the NAMRIA node, including the Maritime Information System for hydrographic and marine datasets, the Environment and Natural Resources (ENR) Mapping Information System for ENR thematic datasets, and the Topographic Mapping Information System for topographic and administrative datasets.

This project ensures continuous upgrades to hardware and the network.  It plays a vital role in improving NAMRIA’s delivery of geospatial information and services by reducing downtime, improving data management, and protecting crucial geospatial assets from imminent cyber threats and dangers.  

The agency continually strengthens its cybersecurity posture by implementing the Data Privacy Act, which includes establishing a Computer Emergency Response Team and enforcing strong access controls and encryption. Additionally, the agency actively invests in research and development to keep its systems resilient, aligns its operations with the National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028, and prioritizes the ongoing upgrading and maintenance of its critical ICT infrastructure, such as the GP, to eliminate vulnerabilities and ensure the reliable delivery of essential geospatial data for government planning and decision-making.

column6: Hydrographic  and Oceanographic Surveys and Nautical Charting
column7: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
column8:
The Hydrographic Surveys Subprogram covers the systematic collection of bathymetric, topographic, and seabed feature data across the country’s maritime zones. These surveys are carried out using NAMRIA’s survey vessels and smaller platforms to ensure comprehensive coverage of national maritime jurisdictions such as the archipelagic and internal waters, ports and harbors, sea lanes, and selected municipal waters. Continuous fuel availability, particularly Automotive Diesel Oil (ADO), remains essential to meeting survey targets. Rising fuel costs significantly impact vessel operations and may reduce the achievable survey coverage without sufficient budget augmentation. Enhanced support for this subprogram will enable NAMRIA to meet its mandated hydrographic data acquisition requirements more effectively.

The Nautical Charting and Maritime Publications Subprogram involves the processing, validation, and transformation of hydrographic data into nautical charts and related maritime publications required by mariners for safe navigation. Updated charts—especially large-scale charts for port approaches—are critical due to the limited maneuvering space in harbors, presence of offshore structures, and various navigational hazards. Over recent years, production has been challenged by the limited availability of updated survey data and budget constraints for field surveys, particularly for busy ports in Visayas and Mindanao. Increased funding for detached hydrographic surveys will directly result in more updated nautical charts, enhancing safety for commercial shipping, fisheries, and other maritime users.

The Physical Oceanographic Surveys Subprogram supports the collection of essential oceanographic parameters such as tides, tidal currents, sea surface temperature, salinity, and density. These data are vital for maritime operations, coastal zone management, disaster risk reduction, and climate-related research. The establishment and maintenance of tide stations—both secondary and subordinate—expand the spatial coverage needed to support hydrographic surveys and improve the accuracy of tide and current predictions. Data gathered through this subprogram feeds into the National Oceanographic Data Center (NODC), which provides critical information for coastal development, navigation, environmental monitoring, and scientific studies.

The Maritime and Ocean Affairs Subprogram contributes to the country’s efforts in asserting maritime rights and supporting ocean governance initiatives. This includes providing technical expertise, hydrographic and oceanographic information, and spatial data to national agencies involved in maritime boundary delineation, marine environmental protection, marine spatial planning, and related policy development. Through this subprogram, NAMRIA ensures that its scientific outputs support national security, environmental sustainability, and compliance with international maritime obligations. Strengthening this subprogram enhances interagency coordination and promotes informed decision-making across the maritime sector.

column4: Transition of ground-based manual measurements to automated measurements and related network aspects
column6: Observing Facilities and Equipment Maintenance Program
column7: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration
column8:
The transition to automated ground-based meteorological measurements is a critical step towards modernizing PAGASA's national meteorological services. Following WMO guidelines and leveraging advanced technologies will enhance our capacity to provide accurate and timely meteorological data. This improved capability is essential for better weather forecasting and climate monitoring, which are crucial in addressing the challenges posed by climate change. Reliable and high-frequency data from AWS will support climate change studies, enhance disaster preparedness, and inform policy decisions that contribute to the sustainable development and resilience of the Philippines.

Investing in a modern AWS network aligns with PAGASA's mission to provide accurate, reliable, and timely meteorological and climatological information and services for the safety and welfare of the people and the environment. The modernization project will:

• Strengthen Disaster Preparedness: By providing high-quality data, we can improve early warning systems for natural disasters, such as typhoons and floods, which are critical in mitigating their impact on lives and property.
• Support Climate Change Studies: Enhanced data collection will facilitate more comprehensive climate research, helping to understand and respond to climate change's impacts.
• Inform Policy and Decision Making: Reliable data will support evidence-based policy formulation and decision-making in various sectors, including agriculture, water resource management, and infrastructure planning.
• Foster International Collaboration: Compliance with WMO standards will ensure that PAGASA's data is compatible with international meteorological networks, fostering collaboration and data sharing on a global scale.
• Enhance Public Awareness and Education: Providing accurate and timely weather information to the public will raise awareness about weather and climate issues, contributing to a more informed and resilient society.

In conclusion, the transition to an automated weather station network is a strategic investment that will significantly enhance the operational capabilities of PAGASA. This project will ensure that PAGASA remains at the forefront of meteorological and climatological services, contributing to the safety, resilience, and sustainable development of the Philippines.

By undertaking this modernization initiative, PAGASA will be better equipped to meet the growing demands for accurate weather and climate information, ultimately supporting the well-being of the Filipino people and the sustainable development of the nation.

column4: Replacement and Maintenance of Hydrogen Generator for Upper-Air Stations
column6: Observing Facilities and Equipment Maintenance Program
column7: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration
column8:
This project involves the design and construction of a dedicated building structure to house and support the operation of Hydrogen Generator system. The facility is approximately 60 square meters in total area, architecturally segmented into two primary, functionally distinct zones to ensure safety, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance

1. Hydrogen Generator Machine
This section is dedicated to the core Hydrogen Generator machine.
Function: Houses the equipment responsible for the electrolysis (or other production method) of hydrogen gas. This are must accommodate the generator unit itself, all associated power supply equipment, cooling systems, and critical control panels. 
Key Design Consideration: The design must account for equipment weight, vibration control, heat dissipation, and adequate ventilation to manage any potential off-gassing or heat load. Appropriate safety features, such us gas detection and emergency shutoff systems, are paramount.
Utility Requirements: Requires robust electrical supply (specific voltage/amperage to be determined), water input (if using electrolysis), and connections for gas output lines to the storage area.

2. Inflation and Storage Area
This section is a regulated, secure zone designed for the management, storage, and transfer of the produced hydrogen gas.
Hydrogen Gas Storage
Function: Houses the high-pressure storage vessels (e.g., cylinders or a bank of cylinders) where the generated hydrogen is buffered and held prior to use.
Design Consideration
- The area must meet strict safety codes for flammable gas storage, including blast-relief walls, explosion-proof fixtures, and robust fire suppression systems. The floor loading must be sufficient to support the weight of the full storage bank.
Inflation Area (or Transfer/Filling Station)
Function: This is the operational bay where the stored hydrogen is safety transferred, typically for filling balloons, fueling vehicles, or transferring to mobile storage units
Equipment: Includes pressure regulators, manifold systems, and filling nozzles/hoses. Clear demarcation and secure access control are essential for this high-risk transfer point.

column4: Integrated Delineation and Resource Mapping Project for Three Legislated Protected Areas in Cagayan Valley (Peñablanca Protected Landscape and Seascape, Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park and Casecnan Protected Landscape)
column6: Protected Area, Caves and Wetlands Development and Management
column7: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
column8:
The project aligns with the objectives of Republic Act 7586, as amended by RA 11038 or the Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System Act, and will significantly contribute to the conservation and sustainable management of the environment and biodiversity by conducting precise delineation of management zones and resource mapping.

Zoning is a key strategy for managing protected areas under RA 11038. It clearly defines areas requiring strict protection and areas that can support regulated human activities. Delineating management zones helps balance ecological preservation with community needs, reduces land use conflicts, and guides enforcement and monitoring efforts.

Resource mapping complements the delineation process by providing essential data on the ecological features, assessing habitat conditions, and detecting threats to ensure that management zones are based on accurate, science-based information. 

Both delineation and resource mapping provide the foundation for sound, adaptive management strategies that protect biodiversity, support livelihoods, and enhance resilience to environmental changes such as climate impacts or resource degradation.

column4: Development of Regional Wildlife Rescue Center in Lantawan Ecopark, Brgy. Crossing, Kitcharao, Agusan del Norte, Caraga Region
column6: Protection and Conservation of Wildlife
column7: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
column8:
The Caraga Region is endowed with rich biodiversity, serving as habitat to numerous endemic and threatened wildlife species. Amid growing threats such as habitat loss, wildlife trafficking, and human-wildlife conflict, the Regional Wildlife Rescue Center (RWRC) located at Lantawan Eco-park, Sitio Little Baguio, Barangay Crossing, Kitcharao, Agusan del Norte, was established as a facility dedicated to the rescue, rehabilitation, and care of injured, confiscated, and displaced wildlife.

However, despite its critical role, the RWRC remains challenged by outdated infrastructure, insufficient quarantine and rehabilitation facilities, and limited staff accommodations. Nevertheless, DENR Caraga remains steadfast in enforcing the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act (RA 9147), ensuring the continued rescue, rehabilitation, and protection of wildlife in the region despite these limitations.

This project aims to advance and strengthen the operational capacity of the RWRC by rehabilitating the existing facilities and constructing new structures to support humane, and science-based wildlife management. Additionally, it aims to transform and enhance the center into a hub for ecotourism and environmental education, further advancing biodiversity conservation, raising public awareness, and promoting sustainable development throughout the Caraga Region.

column8:
Rizal is a province in the CALABARZON region rich in biodiversity. It features a mix of urban and rural areas, with generally hilly to mountainous terrain. It's a forest marked by a mix of natural and protected areas, with a focus on biodiversity and conservation, though it also faces deforestation pressures. Though there are active conservation efforts, the province has also experienced deforestation, with some primary forests lost over time. The issue can be resolved (among others)  with the establishment of additional monitoring stations or lookout towers.

The construction design and other specifications will comply with the DENR-prescribed state Forest Management Bureau (FMB) Technical Bulletin No. 13 

The upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL) is a 26,126-hectare protected area in the province of Rizal and a vital contributor to Metro Manila's water supply and flood control.   It encompasses parts of Antipolo, Baras, Rodriguez, San Mateo, and Tanay and is (as mentioned above) characterized by significant biodiversity and faces threats, thus requires efforts to maintain its ecological functions. 

Lookout towers are relevant for observation and surveillance activities in the field, including fire prevention and early detection, environmental monitoring, and wildlife management.

Proposed sites of establishment are Ayaas Tower-Sitio Mt. Ayaas,  Brgy. Mascap, Montalban; Romil Tower-Brgy.Pintong Bukawe, San Mateo, Rizal;  Sapinit Tower- Sitio Sapinit, Brgy.  San Juan, Antipolo City; Kinapuin Tower- Sitio Kinapuin,  Brgy. Calawis,  Antipolo City, and at Old NGP Area in Scanumay, Sitio San Ysiro, Brgy. San Jose, Antipolo City.

column4: Foreshore Delineation and Profiling for the Province of Iloilo
column6: Management of Coastal and Marine Resources/Areas
column7: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
column8:
Foreshore delineation and profiling  is an areas involves delineating and visually representing the area between the highest and lowest tide lines, essentially the coastal land that alternates between being submerged and exposed by the tide. This process, often involving a Mean High Water Line (MHWL) determination, is crucial for effective coastal management and resource utilization. 
Foreshore delineation  and profiling  is very essential with the following measures:
1. Accurate mapping and manage coastal resources, protecting ecosystem and promote sustainable development.
2. Identify flood-prone zones, informing disaster risk reduction strategies
3. Land use planning, zoning and development decisions, ensuring compatible uses and minimizing conflicts.
4. Environmental conservation such as protect sensitive habitats like mangroves and coral reefs.
5. Promoting eco-tourism and sustainable coastal development.                                                            
6. Effective collection of revenues for developments under foreshore areas
